title: Fast-lane API triage — pocket guide (timeouts, 429s, streaming, error spikes)
content:
Purpose: quick, noise-resistant steps for on-call to make fast, safe choices when surface-level API degradations occur. This is a pocket guide — not exhaustive. Use for first 15–45 minutes of an incident (fast-lane).

Notes to self / framing: prefer quick containment -> visibility -> mitigation -> restore. When in doubt, choose safe degradation (reject non-critical work, fall back to smaller model, disable streaming) over risky rollbacks. Keep user-facing changes minimal.

Channels & tools
- Paging: #sre-oncall and pager duty SRE primary. Ping #ops-prod if customer-impacting and sales/CS need head-up.
- Dashboards: Grafana: API -> request-latency, request-errors, streaming-sessions, token-throughput.
- Logs: Loki / Cloud Logging: filter service=api-gateway OR service=inference-runtime.
- Queries (PromQL) to run quickly:
  - 95th latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="api-gateway"}[5m])) by (le))
  - 429 rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{code="429"}[5m]))
  - stream errors: sum(rate(stream_session_errors_total[5m]))

Top-line fast checks (0–5m)
1) Verify alarm / symptom: what triggered page? timeout/latency spike, burst of 429s, streaming dropouts, OR elevated 5xx. Note the time window and endpoint(s).
2) Scope: global vs region vs customer-specific. Check if traffic is concentrated to a few routes (/v1/generate vs /v1/embeddings) or to a single model.
3) Capacity signals: look at node CPU/GPU utilization, queue depths (inference queue), and autoscaler events.
4) Quick mitigation: enable short-term circuit if one route causing cascade, or switch traffic to fallback model variant.

Decision matrix (one-line):
- Timeouts / latency spike AND high backend queue depth -> reduce batch size / increase workers OR route to dedicated pool. If immediate relief needed, route 20% traffic to smaller model.
- 429s concentrated on one route with steady CPU -> likely rate-limiter misconfig or external client spike -> increase per-route token quota or add short 2s retry-after header.
- Streaming degradation (choppy chunks / disconnects) -> check websocket/ALB connection counts, network errors, and runtime KV cache pressure. Consider switching streaming to poll-based for critical clients.
- Elevated 5xx across models -> suspect runtime regression; if a recent deployment in last 30m, consider rollback and scale down new pods.

Actionable playbook (detailed)
A) Timeouts / high tail latency
- Immediately: reduce client-facing max_seq to 1024 for risky endpoints (use routing config override).
- Check: Grafana latency by model and node. If single node saturated: kubectl describe pod <pod> -n inference; check OOMs or GPU memory.
- Commands: kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep CrashLoopBackOff; nvidia-smi on node if GPU issues.
- If queue backlog > 5000 reqs: enable emergency shed of low-priority work (internal corp batch tasks).
- If rollout occurred in last 1h: escalate to release-eng and prepare rollback PR link.

B) 429s (client-facing rate limits)
- Check rate limiter logs (gateway->ratelimiter). Example query: grep "rate limit" /var/log/gateway/*
- Determine if limits are legitimate (client auth key high-volume) or malfunctioning (bug).
- Short-term mitigations: relax per-key bursts by 2x for 10 minutes for affected clients; add Retry-After header; apply transparent throttling for anonymous traffic.
- Longer-term: bump quotas for high tier customers or tune token-bucket fill rates. Create Jira SRE-req to track.

C) Degraded streaming (lossy, truncated streams)
- Check ALB / LB logs for connection resets. Check websocket proxy health (egress worker counts).
- If KV cache thrash (evictions high) -> increase KV cache size or pin hot prefixes.
- Fallback: convert streaming session to non-streaming mode for that session (emit full final payload and close). Notify SDK owners to support fallback.

D) Elevated error rates (5xx)
- Quick triage: are errors model-specific (runtime stacktrace) or gateway-level (429/504)?
- If model stacktrace points to kernel OOM or quantization error -> mark model variant unhealthy, route to stable variant.
- Collect: last 100 error logs for sample. Attach to incident.

Operational knobs (what we can flip safely)
- Route by model variant: route traffic from big-quant -> small-quant.
- Throttle non-essential routes: /admin/ingest, /analytics-batch.
- Autoscale: increase min replicas for inference-pool in region for 15m windows.
- Enable caching: prefix caching for common prompts (short TTL)

Post-incident quick checklist (first 60–120m)
- Save alert graph snapshot and top 5 queries.
- Annotate Grafana with incident id.
- Share initial summary to #incidents: impact, mitigation, next steps.
- Assign owner for RCA and set 72h follow-up action list (regression test, infra sizing change, quota rule updates).

Open questions / TODOs (draft items)
- How fast can we toggle routing for a single customer? (need runbook with route IDs)
- Add automated synthetic streaming checks that verify chunk continuity every 30s per region.
- Formalize low-priority work categories so emergency-shed logic is predictable.

Appendix: quick command cheats
- kubectl logs -n inference <pod> --tail 200
- kubectl exec -n inference <pod> -- sh -c "ps aux | grep runtime"
- curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}' --max-time 10
- PromQL examples (copy/paste):
  sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="api-gateway"}[1m])) by (code,route)

If you used this doc during an incident: add a short note at top with who ran the fast-lane steps and what the immediate mitigation was. This is a working draft; please comment with improvements (Liam/Gabriel/Sara).

-- Maya
